title: Colony and Protocol Again
premise: Vesper Zhou, the last terraformer on Meridian Station, tends a garden seeded for colonists who will never arrive while recording the colony's quiet collapse in secret logs. When a deep-space vessel returns with its crew aged backward into childhood, Vesper discovers the returning fleet is a fabrication—a protocol designed to keep two hostile fleets believing the other still holds Meridian. To prevent war, Vesper must sustain the lie alongside Ilya, a de-aged pilot who remembers loving them in a future that no longer exists. In the end, Vesper broadcasts the truth along with the garden's living record, choosing memory over protocol, and the fleets stand down—not because the lie held, but because someone finally told them what was worth saving.
about_author: Freya Zhou is a former botanist who spent three years cataloguing seed banks in decommissioned research stations before turning to fiction. She writes slow, luminous science fiction about people who keep tending things no one asked them to save.

chapters.title: The Garden for Unborn Hands
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. We open on Meridian Station's terrarium, where Vesper prunes trees meant for children who were never born and records log entries no one will hear. The colony's population has dwindled to forty; supply ships stopped coming years ago. Emotional beat: tender loneliness, the discipline of caring anyway.

chapters.title: Signal from the Long Dark
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A ship appears at the edge of sensor range—the Aurora Protocol, missing for sixty years. The station's dying council orders it turned away; Vesper secretly sends a landing beacon instead. Emotional beat: reckless hope cracking through resignation.

chapters.title: Children of the Return
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, shifting to Ilya's fragmented memories. The shuttle lands carrying crew aged backward—adults' minds flickering inside children's bodies. Among them is Ilya, who looks at Vesper like they've met. Emotional beat: uncanny grief, recognition without context.

chapters.title: What the Protocol Protects
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Recovering aboard station, Ilya reveals the truth: there are no returning colonists—only a decoy fleet built to convince two armed armadas that Meridian is contested and must not be touched. The de-aging was the price of the long transit. Emotional beat: the weight of a secret that keeps peace.

chapters.title: Two Fleets at the Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both armadas arrive in orbit, each believing the other will strike first if they withdraw. The council wants to surrender the lie and evacuate; Ilya argues the deception is all that stands between them and annihilation. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread, duty tightening.

chapters.title: A Love With No Witness
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya's memories surface fully: in the timeline that was erased, Ilya and Vesper loved each other for thirty years. Now Vesper has never lived those years, and Ilya must decide whether to tell them. Emotional beat: aching asymmetry—loving someone who hasn't loved you yet.

chapters.title: The Lie Begins to Die
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A fleet scout boards the station and nearly discovers the garden is tended by one person, not thousands. Vesper improvises a massacre of small deceptions—empty quarters, borrowed voices—and realizes the lie now requires becoming its architect. Emotional beat: complicity, exhilaration curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Terrarium
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Aurora's failing reactor gives them nine days before both fleets detect the deception. Ilya proposes broadcasting a fabricated evacuation; Vesper counters with something riskier—broadcasting everything, including the logs of the colony everyone abandoned. Emotional beat: moral rupture between duty and truth.

chapters.title: Everything Worth Saving
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, climax. As the fleets power weapons, Vesper transmits the full archive—every death, every abandonment, and the garden itself, live. Silence falls across both bridges. Then, one by one, ships answer not with fire but with their own archives. Emotional beat: terrifying exposure resolving into collective witness.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Months later, the fleets have become an arbitration council; Meridian will be resettled honestly this time. Ilya, aging forward again, asks Vesper to begin again without the ghost of a lost future between them. They plant the first row together. Emotional beat: earned belonging—love chosen freely, memory kept without being ruled by it.
